sections.html: Chickasha is the seat of Grady County, in the south-central part of the state. The county has 55,868 residents and 23,332 housing units, and three of every four homes are lived in by their owners. A typical house sells near $187,900 and was put up in 1981, which is why buyers' inspectors keep flagging aging roofs, wiring and plumbing. Acreage under farm or pasture use fills a big part of the tax rolls. Eleven other towns send their bills through the same Treasurer: Alex, Amber, Bradley, Bridge Creek, Minco, Ninnekah, Norge, Pocasset, Rush Springs, Tuttle and Verden.

Value is the Assessor's job. Billing and collecting belong to the Treasurer, who works from 326 W Choctaw in Chickasha. Call 405-224-5337 on a weekday between 8:00 AM and 4:30 PM.

Ways to pay the Grady County Treasurer
Payment methodFee or note
In personTreasurer's office, 326 W Choctaw
MailSend to the Treasurer's office
Phone with a card405-224-5337
Courthouse drop boxAvailable at the courthouse
Online e-check$1.50
Online debit card$3.95
Online credit card2.95% of the total

Still no statement by the end of November? Phone the office. Each bill stacks county, city or town, and school district levies, so neighbors in different districts can owe quite different amounts.

State law (68 O.S. 2913) lets you pay half or more ahead of January 1 and the remainder ahead of April 1. Fall short of half on the first date and the whole levy goes delinquent on January 1.

For deadlines, the postmark is what counts, with two exceptions: the publication notice and the June resale. A late balance picks up 1.5% a month, assessed on the 16th, and published accounts add fees. When a statement shows BT for back tax, call to learn the real total.

  • Ignoring a statement does not stop the penalty.
  • Publication adds fees.
  • The June resale is the county's sale of delinquent property.

The first move is an informal protest in writing, sent to the Assessor inside 30 calendar days after the valuation notice was mailed. The Oklahoma Tax Commission's Form 974 covers it, along with 68 O.S. 2876.

  1. Fill in Form 974 with your value opinion and back it with sales, comparables or an appraisal.
  2. A purchase within the last two years goes on the form too, with date and price.
  3. Attend the hearing, in person or on the phone.
  4. The Assessor's written decision comes within seven calendar days.
  5. To go further, use Form 976 and appeal to the county board of equalization within 15 calendar days after the decision is mailed.

If the value is unchanged from the year before, the protest window stays open until the first Monday in April. The board should be done by May 31 or whenever it adjourns. Let the 30 days slide and the Assessor's number holds for the year.

sections.h2: Before closing on a Grady County sale
sections.html:
Get the balance from the Treasurer in writing. It may include back taxes, penalties or published fees. Then make sure nothing else is claimed against the parcel.

The Clerk records the deed: $18 on page one and $2 for every page after. Stamp tax runs $1.50 per thousand dollars of consideration, which matches the $0.75 per $500 in 68 O.S. 3201, once the price tops $100. The Clerk's land records are digital from 1929 on, and a deed handed in by 4 pm is filed the same day.

Tax work fits into four stages, and doing it in this order avoids surprises.

  1. Before listing: call the Treasurer for a written balance, and check whether the account carries a BT mark for back tax.
  2. When you have a contract: give the title company the balance and the parcel details. If the house is on acreage, confirm which parts are taxed as farm or pasture land and which as a house lot.
  3. Before closing: ask for an updated payoff good through the closing date, since a penalty of 1.5% per month keeps adding on a late account.
  4. After closing: confirm the deed was recorded with the Clerk, so the next statement goes to the buyer.

If you disagree with your value and the 30 days have not run, filing Form 974 before you list can lower the figure the buyer inherits. It will not change a bill that is already past due, so it works best alongside paying what you owe.

A short call answers most questions. Ask what the current total is and whether it includes back taxes or published fees. Ask whether the first half has been paid and whether the second half is still ahead. Ask for the figure in writing, with the date it is good through. If the property was published, ask what the fees are and how they are paid. If a mortgage company has been paying through escrow, ask whether its last payment posted, since lender payments can arrive close to the deadline.

The same office can tell you how to pay from out of state. Card payments by phone and online e-check payments work for owners who live outside Oklahoma, and the courthouse drop box handles anyone passing through Chickasha.

sections.h2: Selling an older or rural house
sections.html:
A typical seller owns either a house older than the 1981 median or a rural tract. Some inherited it. Others live out of state and cannot easily oversee repairs.

  • Roof and system updates a buyer will ask about.
  • Pasture or crop land that is taxed differently from a town lot.
  • Unpaid taxes with a monthly penalty running.
  • Distance from Chickasha services in smaller towns such as Verden, Norge or Ninnekah.

Farm and pasture land can be taxed differently from a town lot, so a seller with a house on acreage should ask the Treasurer and the Assessor how each part of the parcel is classified. Small-town houses in Verden, Norge or Ninnekah are billed by the same Treasurer as Chickasha homes, but the city and school levies on the bill will differ. Knowing which levies apply helps you explain the bill when a buyer asks where the money goes.

Collect the Treasurer's balance and your deed before any buyer calls, and things move faster. A cash buyer can accept the house as is, yet the tax balance still comes out of your proceeds.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Grady County property tax?
faqs.a: Options are the counter at 326 W Choctaw in Chickasha, the mail, a card payment by phone, the courthouse drop box, or the online tax roll inquiry. The office number is 405-224-5337.

faqs.q: How much is the late penalty in Grady County?
faqs.a: It is 1.5% a month, applied on the 16th, with extra fees once an account is published. Call about any BT statement for the actual total.

faqs.q: How long do I have to protest my Grady County value?
faqs.a: File a written protest with the Assessor inside 30 calendar days of the valuation notice's mailing date. A board of equalization appeal then has 15 calendar days after the Assessor's decision is mailed.

faqs.q: Is a Grady County house worth less because of its age?
faqs.a: The median home here was built in 1981, so age alone does not set value. An older roof or system will matter to buyers, and a Form 974 protest should use sales, comparables or an appraisal.

faqs.q: What if my Grady County tax statement never arrives?
faqs.a: Phone the office if nothing has arrived by the end of November. A lost bill does not stop the deadlines, so ask what is owed before January 1 and April 1.
